correctness.rationale: The proof establishes a complete k-coloured bisimulation invariant on height-two reflexive antisymmetric frames. Degenerate same-colour-only upward cones collapse to terminal types; nondegenerate successor sets have distinguishable characteristic formulas with a depth-two same-colour leaf test. This gives T=q(2^q-1), exactly q2^(q-1) types at depth one, the full Boolean powerset algebra, and a depth-one-indistinguishable pair separated at depth two. The canonical representative is a partial order, and script verifies k=1,2,3; finite checks do not replace infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Actual exact-parameter Published-research and literature searches did not identify the k-variable exact depth filtration for height-two antisymmetric reflexive frames. Agnew proves a local-finiteness criterion, not these finite free-algebra sizes. Bezhanishvili–Ghilardi–Jibladze prove a general S4 one-step construction, but that theorem is for arbitrary reflexive transitive frames of unbounded height including clusters and does not directly imply the explicit restricted depth-two enumeration without a nontrivial specialization and new analysis of the height bound. Prior free-algebra methods could implicitly encompass this computation; historical priority remains a real risk.

value.rationale: Quantitative local tabularity is an invariant of the finite-height modal logic, not an arbitrary count: precise cardinalities and sharp modal-depth normalization bound control the size of free finite semantic test algebras. The construction provides exact atom census at each of three depths, an explicit simultaneously representative coloured Kripke model, and a sharp necessity witness. Unlike qualitative local finiteness, these allow precise bounds on semantic normalization and exhaustive verification for each fixed k.
